_doc: No Justice: the script for the voiced lines (#807). The same shape as sheriff_road.json (its _doc and docs/scripts/README.md say the fields). Nothing is built of this mission yet, so every trigger says what it will need. Nothing here is approved until Sean taps Script OK.
title: No Justice
status: draft: waiting on Sean's Script OK
sources: docs/missions/no-justice.md (Sean's card of 2026-11-09, on PR #743's branch)
docs/story/OUTLINE.md Act I, VOICES.md (Joe, the doctor, Kett, the bold cowboy), SETUPS.md, WORDS.md (A Southern Ute man; rule 7) (PR #833)
#830: C4 a (the raid was provocation; the costume stays), C5 b (the cabin ends Kett's crew), C8 a (the release: P until Sean nods), C13 b (slurs), C14 c
notes: Harlan doesn't speak: he answers Joe with the nod and the shake, and by what he does.

Joe: English is his third language (WORDS.md). Exact, plain, few contractions, says a thing once. Never 'heap', 'many moons', dropped verbs or speeches about the land. His talk with the survivors is in Ute and is not written here: a Southern Ute speaker or not at all.
Nobody says Kett's name (K3, who names him is open). His crew call him 'Red', a cowhand's nickname by look (WORDS.md).
Where Joe and Harlan meet is open (s3); the card says the doctor's office, so that's where it's written. The bold cowboy's part is open (s4): his one line is the card's.

Rule 7 (slurs, Kett one of three men allowed, at a moment that matters): one moment is marked (cabin.bargain) and written without the word. Sean decides whether it gets one; the word is chosen then, and may not be voiceable.

words_to_check.worry: WORDS.md: 'ref' (armed). Look it up before voicing.

setups.status: P: C8 a waits on Sean's nod

setups.what: The outbreak that wasn't (the costume spoils it)
Who sent them (a hint only: Kett offers it, never says it)

cast.name: Joe
cast.bible: VOICES.md, Joe; WORDS.md, A Southern Ute man
cast.brief: Thirties to forties (O), a Southern Ute man; English his third language after Ute and Spanish. Low, exact, unhurried; long quiet, dry humour. Not a film Indian: no stately cadence, no accent played for effect. Cast with care; a Native voice actor if there's ever a choice.

cast.name: The doctor
cast.bible: VOICES.md, The doctor (the same voice as in the sheriff's script)
cast.brief: Late forties, an educated Easterner; brisk, quiet, dry.

cast.name: The bold cowboy
cast.bible: VOICES.md, Smaller voices (s4: his part is open)
cast.brief: Thirties, a Texas hand; plain, blunt, unimpressed by anybody; says the ugly thing because it's true.

cast.name: The red shirt (Silas Kett)
cast.called: nobody names him; 'Red' to his crew
cast.brief: Thirties, a drummer's easy patter on a gunman; light, friendly, quick. Wheedles and whines when cornered; a coward's voice that cracks.

cast.name: Kett's crew (one)
cast.brief: Twenties to thirties, a Texas hand; hard and loud in a fight.

cast.name: Kett's crew (two)
cast.brief: Forties, older and rougher, gravel voice; the one who sees Red run.

cast.name: Rourke's officer
cast.bible: VOICES.md, Rourke; WORDS.md, Soldiers (C8 a, P)
cast.brief: Late twenties, a regular officer, Eastern, correct and cold; whole sentences, never loud.

scenes.title: The doctor's office
scenes.when: After Harlan's sworn (s3: where they meet is open)
scenes.setting: A man in grief in a room you walk into; no quest marker. Joe, the doctor, the bold cowboy. The doctor warns that the killers won't be punished, and the cowboy agrees. Harlan agrees to ride with Joe (a nod).

lines.speaker: doctor
lines.trigger: You come into the doctor's office; Joe is there
lines.delivery: Quiet, to you, with a glance at Joe; he won't tell another man's grief for him.

words.text: This is Joe. The night Earl was shot, his people's camp was raided while the men were out hunting. His wife was killed. I'll not tell the rest. He can, if he chooses.

lines.speaker: joe
lines.delivery: Very level. No heat in it at all, which is what makes it frightening.

words.text: I want the men who did it.

lines.speaker: joe
lines.delivery: A real question; he's watching your face for the answer.

words.text: You wear the sheriff's badge. Does it do anything?

lines.speaker: doctor
lines.delivery: No pleasure in saying it; a man who's sat on juries.

words.text: Bring them in if you like. I never yet saw a white man hang on an Indian's word.

lines.speaker: cowboy
lines.delivery: From the corner, not looking up from rolling a smoke.

words.text: Doc's right. No jury in Colorado'll hang a white man for a Ute woman. I've seen 'em try.

lines.speaker: joe
lines.delivery: Once. He won't ask twice.

words.text: I ride today. Will you come?

lines.speaker: joe
lines.delivery: Already moving to the door.

words.text: Then we go now.

lines.speaker: joe
lines.delivery: No reproach; he expected it.

words.text: No. I did not think so.

lines.note: the card has no 'no' path yet: Joe goes alone?

scenes.title: Joe's camp
scenes.when: The same day, the Southern Ute camp
scenes.setting: The raid's damage still there: burned belongings, bullet holes. The survivors tell Joe what happened, in Ute (not written: a Southern Ute speaker or not at all). Joe tells Harlan, in English, what they said.

lines.speaker: joe
lines.delivery: Getting down from his horse; a hand up to keep you back.

words.text: Wait here.

lines.speaker: joe
lines.trigger: He comes back from the survivors
lines.delivery: Telling it as a list; if he stops on any of it he won't go on.

words.text: Six of them. Seven, one says. They came in the night. We were four days gone, hunting. Four days.

lines.speaker: joe
lines.delivery: The one thing they saw; he gives it weight.

words.text: The one who did it to her wore a red shirt. Faded. That is all they saw of him. It is enough.

lines.speaker: joe
lines.delivery: A plain fact.

words.text: They went toward the hills. That way.

lines.speaker: joe
lines.when: nolaw.followed (you followed Cody out of the saloon)
lines.delivery: He noticed; a question under it.

words.text: You knew that already.

scenes.title: The ride
scenes.when: The foothills, on the raiders' trail
scenes.setting: Joe changes into a cowboy's hat and neckerchief and says why. He leads, reading the trail. They talk a little, without long stops.

lines.speaker: joe
lines.trigger: Before they ride, he puts on the hat and neckerchief
lines.delivery: Matter-of-fact, tying the neckerchief.

words.text: If they see a Ute, they go to the camp after. If they see a cowboy, they come to me.

lines.speaker: joe
lines.trigger: If you look at him a while in the hat
lines.delivery: The first dry joke; nearly a smile.

words.text: A hat and a rag at my neck, and I am nobody's Indian. Only one more man who shot at them.

lines.speaker: joe
lines.trigger: Reading the ground, every so often on the trail
lines.delivery: Half to himself; short.

words.text: Six horses. One throws his right fore.
They stopped here to drink. They were not afraid of anyone behind them.
Fresh. We are close.

lines.speaker: joe
lines.delivery: Out of nowhere, looking ahead, not at you. Then nothing more.

words.text: Eleven years. She could shoot better than me. She told everyone so.

lines.speaker: joe
lines.delivery: Plain; giving you the chance to turn back.

words.text: When I find him, you will not like what I do. Better you know it now.

lines.speaker: joe
lines.trigger: On the hillside above the hideout
lines.delivery: A whisper; counting them.

words.text: Five. Six. There. By the fire. The red shirt.
How do you want it? Quiet, or now?

scenes.title: The hideout
scenes.when: The fight at the gang's camp
scenes.setting: Five or six men, the end of Kett's crew (C5 b). Harlan chooses how it starts: creep in, or open fire. Joe fights beside him. At the first shots, or as it turns, the red shirt runs for the cabin and bars himself in, plain to see. Lines that can repeat have two or three wordings.

lines.speaker: crew1
lines.trigger: They see you, or the first shot
lines.delivery: Shouted, grabbing a rifle.

words.text: Riders! On the hill!
We got company!

lines.speaker: crew1
lines.trigger: In the fight, a man calls where you are
lines.delivery: Short and loud.

words.text: Behind the woodpile!
There's only two of 'em!
By the wagon! Get him!

lines.speaker: crew2
lines.trigger: A man of the crew is hit
lines.delivery: Pain and fury.

words.text: I'm hit! God damn it!
My leg! Jesus!

lines.speaker: crew2
lines.trigger: The red shirt breaks for the cabin
lines.delivery: Yelled after him, as much contempt as fear.

words.text: Red! Where you going? Red, you yellow son of a bitch!

lines.speaker: crew1
lines.delivery: Throwing his gun down.

words.text: I'm done! Don't shoot!

lines.speaker: joe
lines.trigger: Joe in the fight, calling targets
lines.delivery: Short, steady; never shouting more than he must.

words.text: Left. By the wagon.
Two. Behind the logs.
The red shirt. He runs.

lines.speaker: joe
lines.trigger: Joe is hit and goes down
lines.delivery: Through his teeth; annoyed more than afraid.

words.text: I am hit. The leg. Go on.

lines.speaker: joe
lines.delivery: Shaking you off as soon as he's standing.

words.text: Enough. I can walk.

lines.speaker: joe
lines.trigger: You kill the red shirt outside, before the cabin
lines.delivery: Not shouted. Cold, close; then he walks past you to the body.

words.text: That was mine to take.

scenes.title: The cabin
scenes.setting: Harlan forces the door (a kick, or through a wall), Joe close behind. The red shirt is cornered, frightened and unarmed; he surrenders and begs to be taken in. Joe draws his knife and asks if Harlan is going to stop him. The nod answers: nod, I'll stop you; shake, I won't. Stepping between them, drawing on the man or walking out answer too.

lines.speaker: kett
lines.delivery: Too high, too fast; the bluff of a man with no gun.

words.text: Stay out! I got a gun! I'll use it!
First man through that door gets it!

lines.speaker: kett
lines.delivery: Hands up, backing into the corner; grabbing at the badge as a lifeline.

words.text: I'm done! I ain't heeled! You're law, ain't you? Then take me in!

lines.speaker: kett
lines.delivery: Pointing out at the bodies, babbling.

words.text: It weren't only me. Ask them. It weren't only me.

lines.speaker: joe
lines.trigger: Joe draws his knife and walks to him
lines.delivery: Very quiet. To the man, not to you.

words.text: You know me. You were at my camp.

lines.speaker: kett
lines.delivery: The patter back, desperate: selling the one thing he has.

words.text: You'll want to hear who sent me, Deputy, before that Indian opens my throat.

lines.note: Rule 7's moment, if Sean wants one: Kett showing what he is, with the knife at him. Written here without a slur; the word is Sean's call.

lines.speaker: joe
lines.trigger: He turns to you, the knife ready
lines.delivery: Looking you in the eye. Waiting.

words.text: Are you going to stop me?

lines.speaker: joe
lines.delivery: He wants it said plainly, with your head.

words.text: Is that a yes?

lines.speaker: joe
lines.delivery: He puts the knife away slowly. Cold, not shouting.

words.text: Then take him. Take him to your law. We will see what it does.

lines.speaker: kett
lines.delivery: The fear going out of him too fast; already easy again.

words.text: Bless you, Deputy. You're a fair man. I'll come quiet.

lines.speaker: joe
lines.delivery: Wiping the blade; flat. Then nothing for a long time.

words.text: It is done.

lines.speaker: joe
lines.delivery: Staring at you, not the body. A statement, not a question.

words.text: He had his hands up.

scenes.title: The ride back
scenes.setting: Revenge: they ride back together; Joe quieter, nothing mended. Arrest: the prisoner on a horse between them, Joe plainly unhappy, Kett talking.

lines.speaker: joe
lines.delivery: To the road ahead. He knew, and did it anyway.

words.text: It did not give her back. I knew it would not.

lines.speaker: kett
lines.trigger: On the ride back, every so often
lines.delivery: Friendly; the patter of a man who knows something you don't.

words.text: They'll not keep me, Deputy. You know that, don't you?
Fine country. Be a shame to leave it.

lines.speaker: joe
lines.delivery: Not to Kett. To you.

words.text: He talks a great deal for a man with his hands tied.

scenes.title: The jail and the release
scenes.when: Salt Creek, the arrest ending (C8 a: P until Sean nods)
scenes.setting: Kett sits a couple of days in Harlan's jail. Then the train brings Rourke's officer with a paper: a crime against a Ute woman on the reservation is the United States' matter, not the county's. Harlan hands him over on the platform, and the officer turns him loose for want of a witness the court will hear. Later Kett walks Main Street.

lines.speaker: kett
lines.trigger: In the cell, when you come by
lines.delivery: Lying on the cot, hat over his eyes.

words.text: Couple of days, Deputy. That's all this is.
Somebody's coming for me. Not who you think.

lines.speaker: officer
lines.trigger: Off the train, on the platform, to you
lines.delivery: Holding out the paper; courteous and immovable.

words.text: Deputy. I have an order for your prisoner. A crime on the reservation is a matter for the United States, not the county.

lines.speaker: officer
lines.trigger: On the platform, the prisoner handed over
lines.delivery: Not even to you: to the paper. Then he cuts the cords.

words.text: There is no witness a court will hear. The man is at liberty.

lines.speaker: joe
lines.trigger: Joe hears of it, or sees it
lines.delivery: No anger left to show. That's the worst of it.

words.text: Your doctor told you. The cowboy told you. Now you know.

lines.speaker: kett
lines.trigger: You meet him on Main Street after the release
lines.delivery: Tipping his hat. Enjoying it.

words.text: Morning, Deputy. Fine day to be at liberty.
Deputy.
Still here, Deputy? So am I.
